key_insight: EndoVGGT uses a deformation-aware graph attention module to build dynamic, feature-space neighborhoods for depth estimation, restoring geometric continuity in deformable, low-texture surgical scenes.
problem_solved: Overcomes fragmented and inconsistent 3D reconstructions in endoscopic/surgical environments caused by low texture, specular highlights, and instrument occlusions that break fixed-topology methods.
method: Deformation-aware Graph Attention (DeGAT): dynamically constructs feature-space graphs (instead of fixed spatial neighborhoods) to capture local geometry under deformation and occlusion.
Geometry-centric depth estimation backbone that fuses GNN-enhanced features with per-pixel depth predictions to produce coherent surface reconstructions.
Training and inference pipeline tailored for surgical scenes (robust to specularity and occluders) and easily integrated into existing depth/reconstruction models.
impact: Provides a practical way to improve 3D reconstruction robustness for surgical robotics and computer-assisted intervention pipelines, enabling better scene understanding, safer instrument guidance, and higher-quality datasets for downstream AI tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing input endoscopic frame → DeGAT graph construction → GNN-enhanced depth map → 3D surface reconstruction

paper_title: EndoVGGT: GNN-Enhanced Depth Estimation for Surgical 3D Reconstruction
paper_authors: Falong Fan, Yi Xie, Arnis Lektauers, Bo Liu, Jerzy Rozenblit
